title: Sales Engineer (all genders)
description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

AI is fundamentally changing how enterprises operate.

As AI agents become capable of executing increasingly complex workflows, enterprise customers expect more than presentations-they want to see working solutions inside their own environments.

At Lio, we're building THE AI workforce for procurement.

As a Sales Engineer, you're not just supporting sales.

You're helping some of the world's largest enterprises understand what's technically possible with AI. You'll build prototypes, lead technical workshops, and work closely with customers to turn complex requirements into working software that proves real business value.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

In this role, you will:

- Build prototypes, proof-of-concepts, and custom solutions that demonstrate the value of our platform

- Configure and adapt Lio's AI platform to customer workflows and enterprise system landscapes

- Lead technical deep dives, live demos, and workshops with procurement, IT, and architecture teams

- Partner closely with Sales throughout the entire enterprise sales process as the technical expert

- Collaborate with Product and Engineering to translate recurring customer needs into scalable product capabilities

- Travel to customer sites for workshops and technical sessions (1-2 times per week)

- Help shape how enterprise customers adopt AI in complex production environments

YOUR PROFILE

You'll thrive in this role if you:

- Have experience building software. You're comfortable working with APIs, integrations, cloud platforms, or modern development frameworks.

- Enjoy solving customer problems. You like understanding technical requirements and turning them into working solutions.

- Take ownership by default. You move quickly, build pragmatically, and care about delivering measurable customer value.

- Communicate confidently. You're comfortable presenting technical concepts to engineers, IT teams, and senior stakeholders alike.

- Enjoy working across disciplines. You like collaborating with Sales, Product, Engineering, and customers to make complex projects successful.

- Are curious about AI and excited about bringing cutting-edge technology into enterprise environments.

WHAT'S NOT REQUIRED

You don't need experience in procurement software or every technology in our stack.

We're much more interested in strong technical fundamentals, curiosity, ownership, and your ability to solve customer problems than in checking every box on a technology list.

WHY JOIN LIO?

Lio is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and built at Y Combinator. We're bringing Silicon Valley ambition and speed to Munich while building one of Europe's leading AI companies.

From day one, you'll work with Fortune 500 companies across Europe and the US, helping some of the world's largest enterprises adopt AI. You'll build real solutions, influence our product through customer feedback, and work closely with founders, Sales, Product, and Engineering to shape how enterprise AI is deployed.

If you're excited about combining engineering, customer interaction, and cutting-edge AI, we'd love to hear from you.

Any questions about the role? Feel free to reach out to Cansel https://www.linkedin.com/in/cansel-bayram-6a422420b/.

title: Senior AI Engineer
description:
About the role
We are building AI systems that generate production-quality motion from natural language. The system combines frontier language models, an AI generation harness, and a text-native Motion DSL designed for structured, editable animation.
This role spans two connected areas: improving the production generation system used today, and developing specialized models that can generate the Motion DSL directly with higher quality, lower latency, and better cost efficiency.
You will work at the intersection of LLM systems, post-training, code generation, compilers, evaluation, data engineering, and motion design. This is a hands-on engineering role with end-to-end ownership and measurable product impact.
Key Responsibilities
Build and improve production generative systems

• Design and ship improvements across prompt interpretation, model orchestration, routing, retrieval, tool use, structured generation, validation, repair, and visual verification.

• Diagnose recurring failure modes and turn them into durable improvements in prompts, data, system logic, constraints, or evaluation.

• Build compiler-backed feedback loops and deterministic quality gates that prevent invalid or low-quality outputs from reaching users.

• Develop experiments and fixed evaluation batteries that show whether a change genuinely improves output quality.

Train specialized generative models

• Design supervised fine-tuning datasets, training recipes, and post-training experiments for direct Motion DSL generation.

• Explore distillation, preference optimization, synthetic-data generation, reinforcement-learning approaches, and constrained generation where they are the right tools.

• Select checkpoints using robust evaluations across correctness, visual quality, reliability, latency, and cost - not training loss alone.

• Determine whether a model failure is best addressed through data, training, inference, evaluation, or the underlying language/runtime.

Build the data and evaluation foundation

• Turn production generations into high-quality training and evaluation datasets using filtering, provenance, versioning, deduplication, and contamination controls.

• Design train, validation, and evaluation splits that minimize leakage and preserve meaningful generalization tests.

• Create failure taxonomies, hard negatives, regression suites, and representative prompt batteries.

• Combine deterministic checks, model-based judges, render evidence, and human review into a reliable evaluation system.

What we're looking for

• Strong ML and software engineering
You have built and operated production AI or machine-learning systems, not only prototypes. You are comfortable moving across model behavior, data pipelines, APIs, infrastructure, evaluation, and product code.

• Hands-on LLM training experience
You have practical experience with supervised fine-tuning and modern post-training workflows. You understand how dataset construction affects model behavior and can explain how you prevent leakage, contamination, and misleading evaluation results.

• Strong evaluation instincts
You know that generative systems improve only when they can be measured. You can design experiments, regression suites, automated graders, and evaluation datasets that distinguish real gains from noise.

• Experience with structured or code generation
Experience with code-generation models, DSLs, grammars, parsers, compilers, structured outputs, constrained decoding, or program synthesis is especially relevant. The generated output is executable structured code, so syntactic and semantic correctness both matter.

• Production engineering judgment
You treat observability, reliability, latency, inference cost, caching, failure recovery, and maintainability as part of the ML system itself.

• Product and visual judgment
You can distinguish technically valid output from work that feels polished. Experience with animation, motion design, graphics, creative tooling, or multimodal system

title: Staff Tech Lead Software Engineer, Vehicle Realism Platform
locationText: Mountain View, CA, USA; San Francisco, CA, USA
description:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver-The World's Most Experienced Driver™-to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

Waymo’s Simulation Team builds technology that supports the development of the Waymo Driver. It allows the Waymo driver to be tested on millions of miles of traffic before it hits the road. Simulation is crucial to Waymo’s mission of developing the world’s most experienced driver.

The VRP (Vehicle Realism Platform) team builds tools and systems to enable realistic autonomous-driving simulation capabilities across all hardware platforms and diverse driving conditions. VRP manages the interface between the core Simulator Architecture and the physical representation of the vehicle, which includes platform expression, physics, environment, timing, and hardware models in the Simulator. We ensure that signals we get from simulation reflect real-world driving behavior. Our team empowers engineers across Waymo to safely iterate, test, and validate autonomous driving at scale, directly supporting autonomous driving software development, evaluation, and deployment worldwide .

You will:

• Collaborate with onboard and research engineers to expand simulation capabilities and achieve critical Waymo milestones.

• Monitor and improve the reproducibility, reliability, and usability of the Waymo simulator.

• Design long-term architectures to accommodate a growing number of internal customers and product requirements.

• Bridge vehicle subsystems and simulation infrastructure to enhance overall robotic realism.

• Partner closely with collaborators from Simulator, Eval, Hardware, and Onboard orgs, integrating the building blocks they provide and turning them into reliable, reproducible simulation solutions.

You have:

• Hands-on experience building a popular (internal or external-facing) product

• Experience on backend knowledge such as workflows, databases, SQL, debugging, production monitoring, etc

• 6+ years experience in software development

• A strong background in C++

We prefer:

• Experience with the release of software in a highly distributed heterogeneous execution environment

• Experience with systems programming (game engines, database, OS, distributed)

• Experience with robotics or perception systems

• Experience with performance optimization in complex backend and infrastructure systems

• Experience with ML

Формувати та вдосконалювати клієнтські сценарії розвитку споживання продуктів і сервісів екосистеми Київстар.

Формувати стратегії підвищення лояльності, життєвої цінності клієнта (Customer Lifetime Value) та довгострокового зростання бізнесу.

Формувати бачення розвитку функції CBM та забезпечувати його реалізацію.

Розвивати культуру прийняття рішень на основі даних та клієнтоцентричного підходу.

At Fullbay , our mission is simple - to create safer roads for our families and yours. As leaders in the heavy-duty repair industry, we power shops with technology that helps them run smarter and more efficiently. As an AI-First company, we invite artificial intelligence to eliminate friction, spark innovation, and drive efficiencies in every conversation- for our teams and our customers. Fullbay is the number one cloud-based shop management software for commercial repair shops and is growing fast. This is an exciting opportunity to join a high-performing team and help shape the next phase of growth for the company.
Position Overview:
Fullbay runs on a growing portfolio of business applications, and the Integration & Automation Engineer makes them work as one system. You'll design, build, and operate the integrations, data pipelines, and automations that connect Rillet, Salesforce, Masset, Slack, and the Snowflake data warehouse, so data moves reliably, manual work disappears, and reporting can be trusted.
This is a core technical seat inside IT and Security, and an early one. You'll set the standards for how integrations get built, monitored, documented, and secured, all while supporting two parallel product platforms during the migration. The work also lays the foundation for how AI agents access Fullbay 's data, which makes this a chance to shape both how the company runs today and how it uses AI tomorrow.
The Right Wrench for the Job
In a heavy-duty shop, the best technicians know that a truck doesn't run on one good part. It runs because the fuel system, the electrical harness, and the ECM all talk to each other without anyone thinking about it. When one connection fails, the whole rig sits in the bay. That's the work this role owns: the connections nobody notices until they break.
You're the right fit if you take pride in integrations that run quietly, fail loudly, and can be picked up by someone else without a phone call. You're comfortable moving from an API doc to a Snowflake model to a runbook in the same afternoon, you treat credentials and service accounts with the care they deserve, and you're curious about how AI agents will tap into company data in the years ahead.
This isn't the role for someone who needs a dedicated integration team, an established architecture, and a backlog that's already been scoped. If you do your best work when the standards are already written and someone else decides how things connect, this isn't your shop. But if you're energized by building the plumbing from scratch, enjoy partnering with Finance, RevOps, and IT to turn manual pain into reliable automation, and want to help define how Fullbay 's data works for both people and agents, we'd like to talk.

9.具备较强的学习能力，能快速跟进新技术、新公链、新协议，并判断其在业务中的实际价值与落地路径。

title: Senior Software Engineer, Developer Infrastructure
description:
ABOUT SENTRY

Software runs the world and the pace is faster than ever. Sentry helps developers fix errors and performance issues before users notice, so teams can spend less time firefighting and more time building.

Trusted by 200,000+ organizations, Sentry is today’s application monitoring standard and our team is building its AI-native future.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Developer Infrastructure team builds the systems Sentry engineers use to develop, test, and ship software. We own local and cloud development environments, CI/CD across our open-source and private codebases, tooling for creating new services, and SDK and library publishing.

Our goal is to help engineers spend more time building for customers and less time troubleshooting their development tools. You’ll work on problems such as shortening CI feedback cycles, improving deployment reliability, detecting flaky tests, and making development environments easier to use and maintain.

As AI coding agents become part of engineering workflows, you’ll also help our environments, CI, and deployment systems support them with the context and access they need.

You’ll own projects from design through rollout and ongoing operation, working directly with engineers across Sentry to understand their needs and measure whether your changes improve their work.

This role is based in San Francisco, with three days per week in the office to work closely with Platform and Product Engineering teams.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Build and maintain tooling for local and cloud development environments.

- Improve the speed and reliability of CI and deployment pipelines as our codebases and infrastructure grow.

- Develop supported, reusable workflows for creating services and libraries.

- Improve SDK and library publishing tools and release processes.

- Build metrics, dashboards, and flaky test detection to help teams identify and resolve development and deployment problems.

- Give engineers and AI coding agents the context they need to work within Sentry’s systems and conventions.

- Partner with engineering teams to prioritize improvements, support adoption, and evaluate results.

HOW YOU WORK

- You enjoy building tools and infrastructure other engineers rely on.

- You consider reliability, performance, cost, and maintenance when making technical decisions.

- You take ownership from understanding a problem through implementation, rollout, and operation.

- You listen to engineers’ feedback and use evidence to guide improvements.

- You help teams adopt shared tools and standards through clear reasoning and collaboration.

QUALIFICATIONS

- 5+ years of software engineering experience or equivalent experience building developer tools and infrastructure.

- A track record of building or significantly improving developer tooling or infrastructure used by engineering teams.

- Strong proficiency in Python.

- Experience improving CI/CD systems, including diagnosing performance or reliability problems.

- Experience leading complex technical projects through design, implementation, and rollout.

- Experience using Docker and container orchestration in production.

- Experience working with cloud infrastructure such as GCP or AWS.

- Familiarity with Kubernetes and infrastructure as code tools.

- Experience working across engineering teams to build agreement on tools, standards, or workflow changes.

- Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining technical tradeoffs and documenting how systems work.

You don’t need to meet every qualification to apply. If your experience aligns with the core work, we’d like to hear from you.

The base salary range (or hourly wage range, if applicable) that Sentry reasonably expects to pay for this position is $190,000 to $400,000 USD. title: Building Regulations & Permitting Specialist
description:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

- You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

- You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

- Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

- Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

YOUR IMPACT

- You own Proxima Fusion's building regulations and permitting strategy - across multiple sites, from day one.

- Your work spans the Alpha facility permitting process, site development approvals, and the early regulatory landscape definition for Stellaris - a programme horizon broad enough that you will be shaping permitting strategy for projects still being defined alongside those already in motion.

- Permitting is a critical path item, not a support function. You ensure that regulatory requirements are understood early and fed upstream into design and planning decisions - and that Proxima Fusion's relationships with planning authorities are built on solid ground.

title: Manager, Commercial Operations
description:
Manager, Commercial Operations

We are looking for a Manager of Commercial Operations to build and run the transactional engine of the commercial function inside Revenue Operations. ClickHouse runs on a usage-based pricing model, and every deal - direct, marketplace, or partner - has to land correctly in the system: quoted against the right rules, ordered against the right contract structure, and booked cleanly enough that Accounting can bill and recognize it without rework. As we scale the cloud business and widen the product line, that path has to carry more volume, more products, and more deal structures without adding people to the middle of it. This role designs the systems, automation, and controls that make that possible.

Reporting to the Director, Commercial Strategy & Operations, you will own the quote-to-order path and order management, along with the build behind it: the CPQ and quoting system requirements, the automation, the validation and controls, and marketplace transaction operations across AWS, GCP, and Azure. The goal is a commercial path where the standard deal is self-service for the field, quality is enforced by the system rather than by who touched the deal, and human review is reserved for the cases that genuinely need judgment. You will be measured by how fast and how cleanly a deal moves, how little intervention it requires, and how good the experience is for the rep. You will partner daily with Sales, Accounting, Finance, Legal, and Revenue Engineering.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

- Own order management and automate it. Run the intake, review, and processing of quotes, order forms, and bookings to defined SLAs through quarter-end peaks, and continuously engineer the manual steps out of that path.

- Design the quote-to-order flow. Instrument the process, find where it slows or breaks, and redesign it. You own the architecture of the flow, the exception routing, and the automation that makes the standard case hands-off.

- Own the quoting and order management system build. Write the requirements, design the quoting, validation, and approval logic, drive the roadmap with Revenue Engineering, run UAT, and validate every change in production before the field sees it.

- Own the handoff into billing and revenue. Partner with Accounting so that what leaves your process arrives structured, complete, and reconcilable - and build the controls upstream that keep downstream rework from happening at all.

- Build quality in as controls. Validation rules, guided quoting, required-field logic, and automated reconciliation that make an incorrect order hard to submit in the first place.

- Own the field experience of transacting. Treat the rep as the customer: fewer steps, fewer handoffs, shorter quote cycle time, and a standard path that is obvious and self-service. Measure whether it is getting easier.

- Build and run marketplace transaction operations across AWS, GCP, and Azure. Private offers, CSP transactions, co-sell mechanics, and the tooling and automated reconciliation that keep marketplace bookings tied out across the marketplace, Salesforce, and billing.

- Operationalize commercial review. Encode approval rules and guardrails in the system so routine deals route themselves, and escalate the structures that break the system rather than quietly processing them.

- Build the transaction path for new products and acquisitions. Stand up order management, quoting, and the marketplace path for new offerings and newly acquired products, test the flow through to booking before go-live, and be ready to transact on day one.

- Own the integrity of the commercial record. Products, SKUs, pricing, contract terms, and booking attributes in Salesforce, with the controls and monitoring that keep them clean - the forecast and revenue reporting downstream depend on it.

- Instrument and report on the system you own. Cycle time, touch count, SLA attainment, exception and discount volumes, error and rework rates. Use the data t

title: Director, Technology Innovation COE
description:
Our team members are at the heart of everything we do. At Cencora, we are united in our responsibility to create healthier futures, and every person here is essential to us being able to deliver on that purpose. If you want to make a difference at the center of health, come join our innovative company and help us improve the lives of people and animals everywhere. Apply today!

Job Details

JOB SUMMARY:
The Director of Technology Innovation Center of Excellence (CoE) is a strategic leadership role responsible for governing and advancing the evaluation, selection, and deployment of emerging technologies across the supply chain organization. This individual will own and continuously refine a structured stage gate process for vetting technology innovations - ensuring that investments are rigorous, aligned to business priorities, and positioned to deliver measurable supply chain value.

This leader will serve as the bridge between technology vendors, internal stakeholders, and executive decision-makers, championing a disciplined yet agile approach to innovation.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Stage Gate Process Ownership

• Design, implement, and continuously improve a multi-stage gate framework for evaluating, piloting, and scaling supply chain technology innovations

• Define clear criteria, scoring rubrics, and decision checkpoints for each gate (e.g., ideation, feasibility, pilot, scale, sunset)

• Lead cross-functional gate review committees, facilitating structured go/no-go decisions with executive stakeholders

• Maintain a transparent innovation pipeline dashboard, tracking all active and archived technology candidates

Technology Evaluation & Scouting

• Proactively identify emerging technologies relevant to supply chain operations (e.g., AI/ML, robotics, IoT, digital twins, blockchain, autonomous systems)

• Develop and maintain relationships with technology vendors, startup ecosystems, and industry research bodies (e.g., Gartner, Forrester, industry consortiums)

• Conduct structured technology assessments including market analysis, vendor due diligence, and total cost of ownership modeling

• Represent Cencora at industry forums, innovation councils, conferences, and strategic vendor engagements; maintain awareness of supply chain innovation trends and benchmark practices across industries.

Stakeholder Engagement & Governance

• Partner with Supply Chain operations, IT, Finance, Legal, and Compliance to ensure holistic vetting of technology candidates

• Build and manage a Technology Innovation Advisory Board comprising internal subject matter experts and external advisors

• Develop executive-ready business cases and investment proposals for technologies advancing through the pipeline

• Drive alignment between innovation initiatives and the broader supply chain strategic roadmap

Portfolio & Performance Management

• Manage the innovation portfolio budget, ensuring appropriate resource allocation across stages of the gate process

• Establish KPIs and success metrics for piloted and deployed technologies, measure realized benefits including cost savings, productivity improvements and service enhancements and reporting outcomes to senior leadership

• Conduct post-implementation reviews to capture lessons learned and refine the vetting framework over time

Team Leadership & CoE Culture

• Lead and mobilize a cross-functional network of internal stakeholders and subject matter experts, driving innovative outcomes through influence rather than direct authority

• Build trust and credibility across Supply Chain, IT, Finance, Operations, and other functions by demonstrating deep expertise, active listening, and collaborative problem-solving

• Create alignment around a shared innovation vision by engaging stakeholders early and often throughout the stage gate process

• Design and facilitate working sessions, workshops, and forums that draw out subject matter expertise and foster co-ownership of technology evaluation decisions

Senior Product Manager, Athena

As Senior Product Manager, you will own the Athena member experience end to end-from vulnerability intake and submission through validation, remediation, and the delivery of patches and advisories. Your scope will span private feeds, the Chainguard Console, documentation, and customer-facing operations. Rather than owning a single feature, you will bring together multiple teams and related product areas to create a cohesive, scalable member experience.

This is a highly cross-functional role for a product leader who understands deeply technical enterprise customers, can create clarity from noisy input, and is comfortable operating independently in a fast-moving security environment.

What you’ll do

•
Own the end-to-end Athena member workflow and strategy: Define the product strategy, roadmap, and priorities for the member experience, from intake and validation through status visibility, remediation, and how patches and advisories appear in OSV and VEX feeds, private feeds, the registry, console, and documentation.

•
Be the primary product voice: Represent Athena internally and with customers on scope, capabilities, and direction, and educate customer-facing teams so they can communicate clearly and credibly.

•
Turn field input into a prioritized backlog: Identify systemic gaps across the member workflow, convert recurring questions, feedback, and feature requests into clear problem statements, and maintain a well-written, prioritized backlog.

•
Lead cross-functional delivery and technical tradeoffs: Align roadmaps and ownership across Engineering, remediation, Documentation, Customer Success, and other partners; work with Engineering on data validation, workflow routing, entitlements, access controls, and reliability; and partner with remediation on patch delivery, including disclosure readiness, SBOMs and provenance, breaking changes, and capacity tradeoffs.

•
Measure, flag risks, and mentor: Define and report member-experience metrics (submission volume and coverage, time to patch, status visibility, feed adoption), raise customer, delivery, and business risks early (especially around disclosure cycles), and serve as a trusted partner and mentor to product peers.

What we’re looking for

•
5+ years of product management experience, including ownership of a technical B2B product serving enterprise customers in regulated industries; financial-services experience is strongly preferred. Working fluency in software supply chain security, including CVEs, OSV, VEX, SBOMs, provenance, and vulnerability disclosure.

•
Experience leading complex initiatives across multiple engineering and business teams without relying on direct authority.

•
Strong judgment when balancing customer urgency, disclosure timelines, technical constraints, and broader business priorities.

•
Comfort operating with high independence

title: Prepress Operator
description:
LearnTastic is looking for an experienced Prepress Operator to join our production workflow remotely.
You will work closely with our account managers and in-house prepress team to keep moving efficiently, maintain print quality, and meet production deadlines.

Key Responsibilities:

• Review incoming files against tickets, checking trim size, bleed, margins, image resolution, fonts, colour specifications, page count, page order, overprint, trapping, rich black, and missing assets.

• Use Adobe InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop, Acrobat Pro, and Enfocus PitStop to resolve prepress issues.

• Coordinate with account managers when corrections require input.

• Manage PDF proofs, generate and send proofs for approval, implement requested changes, and issue revised proofs until approval is received.

• Prepare press-ready layouts based on press specifications and paper sizes, including step-and-repeat, work-and-turn, sheetwise, booklet signatures, creep adjustments, registration marks, and colour bars.

• Create new layouts when an existing template does not accommodate dimensions or specifications.

• Process approved files through Kodak Prinergy and, where required, Fujifilm XMF, ensuring files are ready for the in-house team.

• Manage production priorities in coordination with account managers, balancing deadlines, approvals, and production requirements.

• Communicate proactively, keep account managers informed of file issues, pending approvals, and potential delays, using email, chat, and phone as needed.

What You'll Need to Succeed:

• At least 3 years of hands-on prepress experience with a commercial offset printing company, either sheetfed or web.

• Proven experience imposing print, and preparing files for production.

• Daily, practical experience with professional prepress workflows and imposition software. Kodak Prinergy and Preps are preferred; experience with Fujifilm XMF, Screen Trueflow, Heidelberg Prinect, or Agfa Apogee is also relevant.

• Strong working knowledge of Adobe InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop, and Acrobat Pro on a Mac.

• Experience with Enfocus PitStop for preflight, PDF inspection, and file correction.

• A solid understanding of commercial print production, including colour separations, CMYK and spot colours, Pantone specifications, overprint, trapping, bleeds, and print marks.

• Good written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate clearly and professionally

• Strong attention to detail, sound production judgment, and the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines independently.

• Reliable internet with speeds of at least 25 Mbps, a backup internet connection, backup power, and a quiet, suitable workspace.
